I've got an HTC M8 on T-Mobile that I just paid off. My 3gb bill will drop from $90 to $60. I have zero coverage at my home and rely on WiFi calling (which I've got to have).

I'm considering moving to Google-Fi for service. It uses T-Mobile, US Celluar and Sprint and also supports WiFi calling. It costs $20 for unlimited phone/texts +$10 per gb. I almost always use under 2gb so my plan would most likely be $40 or less (they credit your bill for unused data).

The catch with Google-Fi is that you have to use a Nexus phone (6P, 5X, or 6). They'll sell you a 5X at a discount ($199 for 16gb/$249 32gb). I'd rather get a 6P but they cost more than I want to pay. You can't buy a used 5X cheaper than buying one new through Google.

Just looking for general advice on the pros & cons of making the switch. Also interested in any other options you can think of--the big issue for me is having access to WiFi calling, which almost no MVNOs (e.g. Straight Talk) offer.

Not many cons of moving to Google-Fi. Lower bill, two extra networks. N5X is a good phone - 6P is better, but either way, you get a stock android experience, quick updates, tons of custom ROM and kernel options.

You could sell your M8 to offset the cost. Swappa is quite good.

Can't think of any cheaper service with Wi-Fi calling. I don't think any MVNO's will provide a femtocell, either.

I thought about Swappa and Gazelle after I made the original post. Gazelle would give me $40 which would help a bit. I guess I could try Craigslist as well. I doubt I'll keep it because I already have a bunch of cheap Android phones laying around.

Wow, $40 is low-ballin' it, though I guess you should expect that from a service like Gazelle. The 32GB variant can still go for over $100 (in good condition). I'd definitely give Craigslist or Swappa a shot before Gazelle.

Waiting a little while might be a good option. Google's $249 deal for the 5X ends Aug. 11th IIRC, but it wasn't exactly the best deal. Just last week, the 32GB variant was going for $240 on eBay (new). We've been seeing more and more deals on both models recently, and with Marlin and Sailfish likely dropping in the coming few months, I'd expect the deals to continue and become better.

I just checked the Swappa prices for the M8 and am kind of surprised folks are still selling them at those prices. I've seen refurb units on Ebay for ~$129 for a long while now. If I were in the market for one, I sure wouldn't pay more than that. That said, I do like the M8 quite a bit--it's an awesome phone. I'd keep using it on an MVNO if any of them offered WiFi calling...but the only one that does (I think) is a Sprint MVNO so that's won't work for me.
